item.title: A further acceleration of clean energy is needed for global CO<sub>2</sub> emissions to peak and decline
item.content:encoded:
Nature Climate Change, Published online: 10 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02821-8

This work projects a decline in global emissions in 2026 as a result of clean energy and in response to conflicts. Energy demand has increased, and will continue to, with electric vehicles and solar and wind deployment mitigating emissions; accelerated deployment is needed to reduce emissions.

item.title: Regional climate change approaches Paris limits
item.content:encoded:
Nature Climate Change, Published online: 09 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02797-5

It has been surprisingly difficult to calculate how much warming different regions of the Earth have experienced since pre-industrial times. Now, research shows that in most land regions, the temperature thresholds that governments agreed to in Paris to keep below are already dangerously close.
item.dc:title: Regional climate change approaches Paris limits
item.dc:creator: Peter Stott

item.title: All IPCC AR6 regions are close to their 1.5 °C- and 2 °C-equivalent warming limits
item.content:encoded:
Nature Climate Change, Published online: 09 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02790-y

Climate targets are set for global temperatures, but what they mean regionally is less clear. Here the authors quantify the amount of human-induced warming in individual IPCC regions and find that, by 2025, they had reached 90–94% (65–76%) of their expected warming levels at the 1.5 °C (2 °C) global warming thresholds.
